## Download the LEOKA data Download LEOKA data and load it into R. Use `read.csv()`
getwd()

capabilities("X11")
capabilities("cairo")

```{r}
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
leoka <- read.csv("/Users/nishiboriryousuke/Desktop/UPenn Courses/crimonology/First hwk/leoka.csv")
```

# Print the first 3 rows of the dataset
```{r}
leoka |> head(3)
```

# How many officers were killed in Ohio in 2007?
```{r}
leoka |>
  filter(State == "Ohio") |>
  select(X2007)
  #2
```
# How many officers were killed in the East North Central region in 2012?
```{r}
find2012 <- leoka |>
  filter(Region2 == "East North Central") |>
  select(X2012)
  
  sum(find2012)
  #2
```

# Add a column showing the total number of officers killed in each state (that is, add up all the years for each state)
```{r}
leoka.sum <- leoka |>
  group_by(State) |>
  mutate(total_killed = rowSums(pick(X2003:X2023), na.rm = TRUE))
  
  leoka.sum |>
  select(State, total_killed)
```
  
# Print the state having the largest number of officers killed (based on total calculated in \#5)
```{r}
leoka.sum |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(total_killed) |>
  tail(1) |>
  select(State, total_killed)
#Texas
```
# Print the region (`Region 1`) having the largest total number of officers killed
```{r}
leoka.sum |>
  group_by(Region1) |>
  summarise(region_total = sum(total_killed)) |>
  slice_max(region_total)
```

# Find all the states that have had no officers killed between 2003 and 2023
```{r}
leoka.sum |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(total_killed == 0) |>
  select(State, total_killed)
```
# In which year and in which state were nine officers killed? (Ideas: \#1 explore `which()` and its `arr.ind` parameter, \#2 explore `pivot_longer()`)
```{r}
library(tidyr)

leoka.long <- pivot_longer(
  leoka,
  X2003:X2023,
  names_to = "year",
  values_to = "killed"
)

leoka.long |>
  filter(killed == 9) |>
  select(State, year, killed)
```


# Sort the regions (`Region 1`) from smallest to largest in terms of the number of officers killed in 2022
```{r}
leoka |>
  group_by(Region1) |>
  summarise(total = sum(X2022, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(total)
```
# Create a bar chart (using `barplot()`) showing the number of officers killed by region (`Region 1`). In addition to your script, upload a Word doc/Google doc that shows you inserting your bar chart into a document using a vector graphics format (SVG or EMF)... not a bitmap image (no JPG, PNG)

Here I put @fig-mybarplot, but I only computed counts for 2023. I need to go back and fix this so it covers all the years 2003-2023. They didn't have R or Quarto documents back in 1764 when I published [_Dei Delitti e Delle Pene_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Crimes_and_Punishments).

```{r}
#| label: fig-mybarplot
#| fig-cap: Number of Officers Killed by Region... incorrectly computed using only 2023 data... to do this correctly I need to figure out the total number of officers across all years

leoka |>
  summarize(tot2023 = sum(X2023), .by=Region1) |>
  barplot(tot2023 ~ Region1, data=_,
          xlab="Region", ylab="Total officers killed")

#| label: fig-mybarplot
#| fig-cap: "Total officers killed by region, 2003–2023"

leoka$total_killed <- rowSums(
  leoka[paste0("X", 2003:2023)],
  na.rm = TRUE
)

region_summary <- leoka |>
  summarise(total = sum(total_killed), .by = Region1)

graphics.off()

svg("officers_by_region.svg", width = 9, height = 6)

barplot(total ~ Region1, data = region_summary,
        xlab = "Region",
        ylab = "Total officers killed, 2003–2023")

dev.off()
```

# Plot the number of total number of officers killed by year
#| label: fig-mybarplot
#| fig-cap: "Total officers killed by region, 2003–2023"
```{r}
year_total <- colSums(
  leoka[paste0("X", 2003:2023)],
  na.rm = TRUE
)

year_summary <- data.frame(
  Year = 2003:2023,
  total = year_total
)

barplot(total ~ Year, data = year_summary,
        xlab = "Year",
        ylab = "Total officers killed",
        las = 2)
```


# Which region (`Region2`) showed the largest percent decrease in 2023 over the average of 2003-2022? (Lots of directions to go here. Perhaps first consider making a new variable that has the 2003-2022 totals in each row. Then consider `pivot_longer()`/`group_by()`/`summarize()`)

```{r}

leoka$total_killed1 <- rowSums(
  leoka[paste0("X", 2003:2022)],
  na.rm = TRUE
)

region_summary <- leoka |>
  summarise(
    total_2003_2022 = sum(total_killed1),
    killed_2023 = sum(X2023, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = Region2
  )


region_summary$average <- region_summary$total_2003_2022 / 20


region_summary$percent_decrease <- (
  (region_summary$average - region_summary$killed_2023) /
    region_summary$average
) * 100

region_summary |>
  arrange(desc(percent_decrease))
#1     South Atlantic
```
